result:
I’d make a safe childhood universal.

Not a perfect childhood, or one without disappointment. Just one where no child has to wonder whether they’ll eat, whether someone will hurt them, or whether there’s anyone they can trust.

So much of what goes wrong in the world starts with people learning, very early, that survival requires fear or cruelty. I’d change that first lesson—not because it would fix everything, but because nobody should have to spend their whole life recovering from the beginning of it.
